relationships.subject: C-LTMRs
relationships.evidence_quote: In the mouse, we found that C-LTMRs express high levels of Nav1.7.

relationships.subject: Nav1.7
relationships.evidence_quote: Genetic loss or selective pharmacological inhibition of Nav1.7 in C-LTMRs resulted in a significant reduction in the total sodium current density, an increased mechanical threshold and reduced sensitivity to non-noxious cooling.

relationships.subject: PF-05089771
relationships.evidence_quote: Small molecule blockade of Nav1.7 significantly reduced the total sodium current density in C-LTMRs

relationships.subject: Nav1.7
relationships.evidence_quote: Nav1.7 is therefore not only essential for normal pain perception but also for normal C-LTMR function, cool sensitivity and affective touch.

relationships.subject: C-LTMRs
relationships.evidence_quote: all C-LTMRs express the VGSC Nav1.8

key_findings: Nav1.7 loss in humans (CIP) impairs affective touch; mouse C-LTMRs express high Nav1.7.
C-LTMR-specific Nav1.7 KO or PF-05089771 reduced sodium current, raised mechanical threshold and impaired cool sensing.
